inputs.net_debt_note: H1-2026 (30-Jun-2026) balance sheet: TotalDebt 73,525 (borrowings + IFRS-16 lease liabilities ~19,300) less own CashAndEquivalents 15,137. Excludes $20.0m restricted Clearing House risk capital and ~$24.8m funds held on behalf of third parties (offset by an identical liability) on both sides. Company-defined net debt of $39.1m excludes lease liabilities; ours includes them (leases-as-debt treatment). H1 cash is a seasonal low (FY-end cash runs ~2x higher on annual listing-fee collection) - the choice of the June balance sheet is conservative by roughly 4-5c/share.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report cash flow reconciliation (share-based payment expense); SBC is expensed within statutory EBITDA/NPAT, so the ebitda_margin driver is stated pre-SBC and SBC deducted as its own line to keep the house SBC row explicit without double-charging
inputs.share_count_basis: 329,241,123 shares at H1-2026; diluted EPS equals basic (6.5c FY2025) so dilution is negligible; held FLAT - SBC (0.7% of revenue) is fully expensed in the flows
inputs.mid_cycle_fcf_note: Normalised unlevered owner FCF at FY2025 scale: (normalised EBITDA 53,500 - SBC 1,000 - capex incl ~1.4pp lease-asset renewal 13,600) x (1-28%) ~ 28,100, plus ~1,500 of temporary amortisation tax shield (D&A 19.0m vs cash capex 11.6m - the NZXWT 'amortisation bubble' management itself flags) ~ 29,500. Used instead of any single-year print: reported FCF spans -17,060 (FY2022, inflated by the $25m SuperLife management-rights acquisition booked through investing) to +27,854 (FY2025, near-peak). The model's Y1 FCF of 30,088 is component-built off FY2026 guidance, not an extrapolation of the FY2025 print, and its 19.2% margin is BELOW FY2025's actual unlevered margin (~21%).

inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (SKILL.md routing: operating company - fee/commission revenue, genuine EBITDA and FCF; exchange + funds management + wealth-platform SaaS). Section 7 adaptations applied: (a) NZD WACC from NZD risk-free + ERP; (b) leases treatment A - lease liabilities in net debt, NO deduction of lease principal from flows, ongoing lease-asset renewal (~1.4pp of revenue, ~ROU depreciation run-rate) charged inside the capex%% line; (e) SBC near-zero (0.7%% of revenue) - rows kept explicit, house/street band collapses to ~5c and band_position is null; (f) risk charged once - single 9.5%% WACC across all scenarios, cyclicality and issuer-attrition risk live in the scenario flows, the small-cap illiquidity premium (1.25pp) lives in the discount rate only. REVENUE BASIS BREAK: H1-2026 restated revenue to a gross basis (+5,894 H1-2025, +12,303 FY2025; profit lines unaffected). The model is DRIVEN OFF EBITDA/NPAT/FCF, which are basis-consistent across the whole series; forward revenue projects from the FY2025 gross-basis 141,251 so margins are internally consistent; historical revenue CAGRs are computed on a restated NET basis (FY2025 net = 128,948). The FY2024->FY2025 margin fall (20.8%%->15.2%% net margin) is presentational, not deterioration. FY0 unlevered FCF ties: reported FY2025 FCF 27,854 is levered (after ~3.4m net finance); unlevered equivalent ~30.3m vs component-built Y1 30.1m. Interest income not stripped (net-debt company; own-cash interest immaterial, clearing-fund interest is operating).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: ebitda_5yr_cagr (8.5%) moderated for flat-to-declining Markets segment; EBITDA/NPAT/FCF are the basis-consistent series across the FY2025 revenue restatement
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue CAGRs computed on a RESTATED NET basis (FY2025 = 128,948, i.e. 141,251 less the 12,303 gross-up) - a raw FY2024->FY2025 comparison would manufacture ~10pp of phantom growth. Equity 5yr CAGR (12.6%) is inflated by the 2021-22 capital raises (shares 281m->315m) and the ~10.4% revenue CAGR is partly acquired (QuayStreet, SuperLife rights); EPS 5yr CAGR is ~0.7% because FY2020 was a COVID trading-activity peak. None of these is a clean organic growth anchor - hence EBITDA-based selection.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR undefined (FY2022 owner FCF negative on the $25m acquisition-inflated capex). SBC-adjusted vs reported FCF CAGRs differ by <0.3pp - SBC is not a swing factor here.

assumptions.wacc_rationale: NZD-built, matching NZD flows: NZ 10-yr govt risk-free ~4.4% (mid-2026) + 0.9 beta x 5.0% NZ ERP + 1.25pp small-cap/illiquidity premium (NZ$505m cap, thin NZX liquidity) = ~10.15% cost of equity; after-tax cost of debt ~4.3% (6.0% pre-tax, 28% NZ corporate rate); weights ~90% equity / 10% debt at market values -> WACC ~9.5%. SINGLE WACC across scenarios - Markets-segment cyclicality and issuer attrition are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not double-counted in the rate.
assumptions.tax_note: NZ statutory 28%, flat - no NOLs, credits or abnormal items in the FY2025 rate

base.narrative: FY2026 lands mid-guidance (EBITDA $53.0-58.5m pre project costs; H1 $27.3m on track). Revenue +11% in FY2026 (H1 actual +13.3% on a like-for-like gross basis, boosted by a one-off wholesale FUM mandate), decaying to 2.25% terminal. Smart FUM compounds with the KiwiSaver pool (contribution rate 3%->3.5% Apr-2026, ->4% Apr-2028; management targets $20b FUM by 2029) and NZXWT scales with the Craigs migration (live 2027), while Markets stays flat-to-slightly-down as delistings (Restaurant Brands, Vital, Marsden Maritime within 14 months) roughly offset listing-fee pricing and data growth. Statutory EBITDA margin drifts 34.5%->36.0% as Smart passes the $15-20b peak-efficiency scale, partly offset by passive fee compression. D&A converges from 13.4% to 9.2% of revenue as the NZXWT amortisation bubble rolls off - the terminal year does NOT perpetuate the temporary tax shield. Ebitda_margin_path is stated PRE-SBC (statutory = path minus 0.7pp SBC).

bull.narrative: The policy tailwinds convert: KiwiSaver contribution increases proceed and 'asset recycling' (partial listings of state/council infrastructure) refills the IPO pipeline; Smart reaches $20b+ FUM early with genuine scale margin expansion; the Craigs custody migration and the $275b funds-registry addressable market make NZXWT a second profit engine; NZX20 futures and dairy derivatives build liquidity; new CEO Mirza's 'scale, liquidity, global relevance' agenda lands. Margins expand to ~38.5% statutory.

bear.narrative: Issuer attrition accelerates - ASX (4x capital pool; its NZ-linked daily turnover already exceeds NZX cash-market turnover) keeps pulling listings and liquidity, the IPO pipeline stays unconverted through the NZ cycle, and delistings compound the liquidity spiral in the highest-margin Markets segment. Passive fee compression outruns FUM growth at Smart (H1-2026 Smart margin already fell 45.4%->42.2% ex-project costs despite +19% revenue) and 'one-off' restructure costs stay permanent. Growth fades to ~1% and statutory margin erodes to ~32.5%. Balance-sheet risk stays low - this is a stagnation bear, not a solvency bear.

entry_price.note: A 15% NZD hurdle is demanding against a 9.5% WACC for a mature income stock - the weighted buy-below price of ~$0.83 sits near the stock's decade low ($0.982). At the current price the base-case implied return is ~8.3% (see required_return_table: value equals price between the 9% row and WACC row).

required_return_table.note: 9.5% is the model WACC. Current price NZ$1.535 exceeds even the 9% value - on base-case flows the market is accepting roughly an 8.3% NZD return, or is pricing something between base and bull.

sensitivity.note: Rows = WACC, columns = terminal growth (base scenario's 2.25% +/-1pp in 0.5pp steps). Flat cells are where the 15x terminal FCF cap binds (all of the 7.5% WACC row; high-g cells at 8.5% and 9.5%).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the bear axes are live, not hypothetical - three delistings in 14 months, a decade of failed listings growth conceded by the incoming CEO, ASX turnover in NZ-linked stocks already above NZX's, and Smart margin compression visible in H1-2026. Bull trimmed to 25% because it requires several independent policy/execution outcomes (KiwiSaver increases AND asset-recycling IPOs AND Craigs-scale platform wins AND an unproven new CEO) to land together. No solvency risk in any scenario, so bear is not weighted higher.
probability_weighted.band_note: House/street band is ~NZ$0.05 wide (SBC is 0.7% of revenue - effectively an SBC-zero market), narrower than estimation error, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate figure.

sanity_check.iv_vs_decade_price_band: Weighted IV NZ$1.27 and all three scenario IVs (0.83 / 1.28 / 1.69) sit inside or at the edges of the 10-year traded range $0.982-$2.082; current $1.535 is mid-range and the model says fair value is toward the lower third of that range.

implied_pe.history: 10-yr Dec-close P/E on derived EPS (NetIncome/shares - EPS column is in CENTS): FY2016 31.6x, FY2017 20.1x, FY2018 23.0x, FY2019 25.7x, FY2020 31.8x, FY2023 25.6x, FY2024 19.3x, FY2025 23.0x; band ~19-32x, median ~24x. Weighted IV implies 19.4x - the bottom edge of the band.

implied_ev_ebitda.history: ~10.3-16.6x over the decade (FY2018 10.3x, FY2024 11.5x, FY2025 10.5x, FY2020 peak 16.6x) on statutory EBITDA; weighted IV implies 8.9x normalised EBITDA - slightly below the decade low.
implied_ev_ebitda.assessment: Defensible rather than alarming: the historical band's floor was set in a lower-rate regime and the market has persistently paid a national-infrastructure scarcity premium (compare AIA.NZ). The model instead charges live issuer attrition and a 1.25pp illiquidity premium in a 9.5% NZD WACC. The gap between IV ($1.27) and price ($1.535) IS that scarcity premium plus ~1pp of discount-rate disagreement - see required_return_table.

implied_pb.history: 3.5-8.3x over the decade (FY2022 3.5x, FY2024 4.0x, FY2020 8.3x); weighted IV implies 3.4x - at the historical floor.

sanity_check.peak_fcf_check: Base year is NOT the FY2025 peak print: mid_cycle_fcf 29,500 is component-built (see inputs.mid_cycle_fcf_note); Y1 owner-FCF margin 19.2% is below FY2025's actual unlevered ~21%; FY2022's -17,060 trough is acquisition capex, not operations.
sanity_check.exit_multiple_check: Implied exit multiple 14.1x terminal FCF (base) vs ~19x EV/owner-FCF today - the model assumes multiple CONTRACTION, not expansion.

valuation_philosophy: NZX is an income-plus-modest-growth franchise, not a compounder: dividend 6.1c flat FY2016-FY2024, 6.3c FY2025 (fully imputed), payout ~100% of statutory NPAT / ~80% of normalised FCF under a 70-90%-of-FCF policy - so retained capital for reinvestment is minimal and value accrues as yield plus the KiwiSaver/FUM growth engine (Smart + NZXWT, ~49% of revenue, growing high-teens) dragging a flat, slowly-leaking Markets monopoly. At $1.535 the net yield is 4.1% (~5.7% gross of imputation for NZ holders) plus ~3-4% medium-term growth - roughly a 8-9% NZD total return, which is why the price sits above a 9.5%-WACC DCF. The house model prices the equity at ~$1.27: buy the yield when the price also clears the discount-rate bar, i.e. toward the bottom third of the decade range. Terminal growth 2.25% reflects a mature, small, single-country franchise.
